newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl disatisfied with Germany's Expo 2000-paper.
newsitem.headline: Kohl disatisfied with Germany's Expo 2000-paper.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl is pressing German industrialists to get involved in Hanover's Expo 2000 World Trade Fair.

Many industry leaders knew the importance of the exhib's central theme, the relationship between economies and the environment, but had not yet shown willing to take part, Kohl told the business daily, Handelsblatt in an interview being published on Thursday.
"This involvement must be stepped up considerably," Kohl said in remarks ahead of a meeting on Thursday with business and industry leaders.
He said it would be an opportunity for the German economy if companies were to show their technical know-how to an audience of millions of people from all over the world.
Handelsblatt said that of 189 countries invited to participate in the event in the northern city of Hanover, 129 had agreed to take part.

Kohl said this was more than the number of participants in the last Expo world trade fair in Seville, but added that he hoped other important countries such as the United States, China, Australia and New Zealand would agree to join.
